key_insight: LLM agents can act as a reliable natural-language interface for home energy scheduling, achieving near-optimal appliance plans when paired with tool calling and live energy data.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical path to make HEMS more user-friendly while preserving cost savings, demand-response flexibility, and safety constraints.
method: Tool-calling ReAct agent for multi-appliance scheduling
Uses live Octopus Agile prices, weather forecasts, PV estimates, usage data, and retrieval-augmented knowledge
Benchmarked GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 against MILP ground truth
evidence_signal: Across tariff, conflict, solar-cooptimization, and week-long tests, native function calling yielded 100% scheduling success and 96.7–98.0% of oracle savings.
watch_item: Text-parsed action interfaces are much less reliable than native function calling, so deployment depends on robust tool integration and constraint handling.
paper_title: LLMs for Agentic Home Energy Management
